title: M7.P5: Define a thin rolling RC and release naming policy
body:
## Qualification reconciliation — 2026-10-11

Shared #530 installed proof now verifies the selected thin naming policy on assembled engineering firmware: metadata, filenames and reviewed clean/retained INFORMATION frames match source1a02664844 and UTC194522. The existing57 host controls cover public RC/release examples; engineering dev is not a public RC. See [corrected clean/upgrade qualification](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/b990d32c935c557ba8808cfedb7344730eee60fe/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-11-pixelelated-replacement-20). Publication remains #265/#528.

The earlier remaining-work statements below are historical; the acceptance checklist is reconciled to the evidence above. No owner device/cloud action or publication occurred.

## Maintainer request — 2026-10-10

> This seems like a good fix to take care of before we generate our next potential release candidate build. We should think of a task around how precisely we want to name these builds. If it is a rolling release, we might not need too many names. We might just have release candidates and releases and nothing else. For example, I'm not sure we need alphas and betas yet if we want to keep our release pipeline thin. We should think of what other issues have come up beyond 5.30 and 5.31 that we might want to address with this next release candidate.

## Current behavior and scope

Parent #265 owns versioned publication. #530 is delivered on next at f10eec13067a69e3a5670a0879736801b40d2fc0; its assembled-image criterion remains open. D-WORKFLOW-157 and docs/releases/versioning.md separate release version from UTC timestamp/source hash, preserve immutable artifacts, and default unqualified engineering builds to dev. Optional alpha/beta/rc syntax is supported, but no progression is required.

D-WORKFLOW-159 now selects public RCs (0.0.1-rc.N) and releases (0.0.1, then0.0.2), with short matching tags/titles and UTC/source build metadata retained. dev is engineering-only. Positive N starts at1 per base and is consumed by every new frozen coordinated source/timestamp set, including failures; no reuse. RC-to-release reassembles embedded metadata into new bytes/manifest and receives required qualification. No automatic designation/promotion/publication.

This is a focused policy/implementation child, not a second versioning system or permission to publish. Do not expand it into release automation for hypothetical future channels. #531's USB consumer must be corrected regardless of the naming choice.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes. Host fixtures verify name/tag/sidecar derivation and negative cases; actual image metadata and INFORMATION frames verify the selected convention on the next guest. No owner device or cloud action is required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A documented decision and examples cover the two proposed public states, the RC counter/reset, rolling patch increments, and the distinction between unqualified engineering builds and qualified candidates; docs/releases/versioning.md, #265 and M7 agree. Alpha/beta stages are not prerequisites.
- [x] Retained executable controls show consistent firmware filenames, /etc/os-release, identity sidecars and GitHub tag/title/prerelease state for RC and release examples, including two same-day builds and malformed/duplicate identities. Build metadata is not used as version precedence.
- [x] The chosen RC-to-release transition explicitly accounts for the embedded version and exact byte/manifest identity. A rebuild receives its own identity and required qualification; renamed or retagged firmware is never presented as unchanged qualified bytes. Published tags/assets remain immutable.
- [x] The next assembled candidate's metadata and reviewed INFORMATION frames match the policy and its source identity. Any changed screen content updates the canonical flow/frame index; #530 owns the shared installed-identity proof rather than duplicating it.

Actual release publication remains #265/#344 and #528. This issue does not waive source, VM, audit, hardware or named publication gates.


## Implementation — 2026-10-11

The maintainer: "Let’s process with 532 then 533". Proceed serially: select the thin policy and qualify its host contract before the #533 reconciliation. Public versions/tags are 0.0.1-rc.N / v0.0.1-rc.N and 0.0.1 / v0.0.1. Engineering defaults remain dev and cannot produce a public release plan. No alpha/beta stages. RC N starts at1 for each base version; each newly frozen build set consumes the next value, even if it fails; one coordinated source/timestamp set shares N across targets. Rolling releases increment patch. RC-to-release reassembles embedded metadata with a new identity and its own required qualification, never relabels RC bytes.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes; these changes are host assembly/release-plan logic. Run actual identity/name/os-release/sidecar blocks and the actual manifest verifier/planner in synthetic host fixtures for RC/release, same-day sets, forbidden stages, duplicate output and tampering controls. Keep the final assembled-image/frame criterion open under #530. No new VM boot or personal device/cloud operation is required for these host controls.


## Qualified host policy — 2026-10-11

57 actual host controls pass; docs/qa-logs/2026-10-11-release-policy/ retains original results and source hashes. First harness failed on a stray temporary etc directory in a flat bundle; original21/2 remains. Corrected fixture uses the unchanged real verifier, with duplicate-file preservation and malformed/dev/alpha/relabel/tamper refusal. No actual image or VM run is claimed. First three criteria satisfied; the final installed metadata/INFORMATION criterion stays open and shared with #530. Source delivery is being prepared; #533 now proceeds.


#533 readback: policy source40bc5469b9 is committed. Host57/57 controls qualify the policy only; #530/#532 installed-image and publication gates remain open. The original #530 general prerelease support is narrowed by #532 to dev, rc.N or release.
